To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 261 bp segment of the rat β2‐adrenoreceptor gene 5′ flanking region (−1,335 to −372, start of translation at +1) is sufficient to direct high levels of expression of the β2AR gene in fetal liver and that a repressor element located within this 261 bp segment is responsible for the decline in expression of the βAR gene in the liver of the developing rat.

the β2‐AR promoter is sufficient for high expression in the fetal liver and that a repressor element, located upstream from the promoter, is responsible for the decline in β2AR gene transcription during the first 3 weeks of postnatal development.

The β2‐adrenoceptor gene is transcriptionally suppressed in rat liver during early postnata development, and this suppression is mediated by a repressor element that is located in the 5' flanking region of the gene.

understanding the mechanisms that control the expression of the β2AR gene in rat liver during the first 2 weeks of postnatal life, a time when there is a decline both in transcription of the gene and the number of receptors.

the transcriptional regulation of the β2 adrenergic receptor (β2AR) gene in rat liver undergoes a developmental switch that is controlled by the presence of an upstream repressor.
